Discord puts the author of a quoted message among the mentions: a moderation command typed with NO target, as a reply, therefore aimed at that person. Three batches had closed the door command by command. The essential part was missing: the list of protected commands was copied by hand into the tests, so a command added tomorrow could arrive unguarded with nothing to flag it. The count is now taken from the code itself — all 29 commands that designate someone are either guarded or listed with the REASON that exempts them and the code shape that makes that reason true. And the rule, which existed in SIX copied versions (two had already drifted apart), is now written in exactly one place.
  • 🗄️ A snapshot of a wiped channel can no longer come back out of an old backup. Before clearing a channel, the bot keeps a six-hour snapshot of it so the channel can be restored — names and message text included. That snapshot was already excluded from server backups, but RESTORING one brought it back: a backup made by an earlier version of the bot rewrote up to 120 KB of members' messages per channel, under keys pointing at channels that no longer exist, hours after the six-hour window had closed. The intent was written in the code — "nor to come back out of a restore" — but the rule existed in two copies and only one of them had learned to recognise those snapshots. Now there is only one.
  • 🛡️ A deleted channel no longer disarms the quarantine brake. A quarantined member may only post at intervals; beyond that their message is deleted and they get a reminder. That reminder was posted in the channel — and if the channel had just been deleted, the send failed, the error was swallowed, and the brake reported "message not braked". The quarantined account therefore slipped through, with nothing in the logs. The reminder is a convenience, the braking is the rule: if the channel is gone, the bot stays quiet and brakes anyway.
  • 📍 A deleted channel can no longer trip up message handling. For the bot, "the channel a message is in" is not a fixed value: it is a lookup in its memory, redone on every read — and it returns nothing as soon as the channel has been deleted. One game already paid for this: the channel lock was never released, and the command kept answering "a game is already running" until the next restart. The last six places that read the channel that way just to get an id now read the id carried by the message itself, which cannot disappear.
  • 🪜 « I grant myself full powers, then I empty the server » is now rehearsed before every update. This is the other half of sabotage: the previous check destroys channels and roles, this one goes after people. 29 protections watch that path — when someone receives a role, when a member is banned, when a member leaves — and none had ever run outside production. The bench now pushes: an administrator role handed to a three-day-old account, a role handed to someone you blocked with +blrank, the bot being neutralised by having its own rights stripped, then eight bans and eight kicks in a row. Verdict: the blocked person does not keep the role, the owner is never punished, nothing crashes.
  • 🛡️ A channel deleted while a message is being processed no longer cuts automoderation short. The bot re-read the channel at every step — and a deleted channel (or simply one dropped from its cache, which happens to threads every hour) made the current step fail and every step after it: the warning never went out, and the rest of the message’s filters were abandoned silently. The channel is now held once, when the message arrives, so the protections already written against failed sends finally do their job.
  • 🚪 Lifting a sanction will always stay at least as hard as applying one. The day you tighten who can sanction, it is easy to forget who can lift it — and the sanction becomes decorative: someone who cannot ban must not be able to unban. The rank check was already verified for every lifting command; the permission TIER was only compared for a single pair. Every command that lifts a sanction is now compared to the one that applies it, with no exception — and the only exemption from the rank check (unban, since the person is no longer on the server) is re-verified every time, so it cannot outlive the reason behind it.
  • ✏️ Editing a message to slip in a banned word no longer escapes the sanction. The word was deleted, but in one precise case the author was not punished: if the channel left the bot's memory during the deletion, the warning posted to the channel failed — and it took the sanction down with it, because the sanction came AFTER. Nothing reported it. This is exactly the path of someone who posts a clean message and then edits it to get around the filters. The bot now deletes, punishes, and only then warns: a failed warning can no longer undo a sanction.
  • 🎁 The voice gift winner is congratulated in THEIR voice channel’s chat, no longer by direct message. The announcement goes to the text chat of the voice channel they were drawn from, and mentions them: only they are notified, even if the configured prize contains an "@everyone". If the bot can’t write in that chat, it doesn’t fall back to a DM: the prize stays credited, the trace stays in the logs, and +vcgift says so instead of announcing a hand-over that never happened.
  • 🛡️ +temprole no longer lets someone grant a role above their own. The hierarchy check read the moderator from the bot's memory, and if they weren't in it at that moment, the check was simply skipped: a delegate could then give themselves, or someone else, a role placed higher than theirs. On custom bots, that memory is cleared every hour. The bot now fetches the moderator from Discord, and if it cannot verify their rank, it refuses.
  • 🛡️ The rank check that guards every sanction no longer opens up when the bot can't tell who asked for it. Before banning, kicking, muting or warning, the bot checks that the moderator ranks above the target — and that the target isn't the server owner. In a rare case, when the bot couldn't find the moderator at the moment of the check, that check was simply skipped, owner protection included. It now refuses the action as a precaution and asks to try again.
  • 🎫 A forbidden role didn’t always stop someone from opening a ticket. +ticket interdit blocks opening for holders of a role (often put on someone abusing support), and +ticket requis reserves it for holders of another. Both checks read roles from the bot’s temporary memory — and when the member wasn’t in it anymore, they checked nothing: the ticket opened. They now read the roles Discord sends with every click. If those roles are truly unreadable, opening is still allowed, so support is never closed to everyone.
  • 🎭 +massrole "Replace A→B" no longer makes anyone lose a role when an add fails. The bot removed A before adding B: if the add failed for a member (the bot’s role moved during a long operation, the member left in the meantime), that member ended up with neither role, and the report only spoke of "failures". B is now added first: on failure, the member stays as they were, or keeps both roles — nothing is ever lost, and running "Remove A" again finishes the job.
  • 🗑️ +backup restore … purge no longer deletes anything when it doesn’t know what to spare. Purge removes channels missing from the backup, sparing the ones the bot manages (quarantine, reports, tickets…). If the list of those channels couldn’t be read, it stayed empty — and the purge then deleted the quarantine channel too. Now, without that list, no channel is deleted and the report says so at the top; the rest of the restore runs normally.
  • 🧱 Tickets and voice channels can no longer fill a server up to Discord’s limit. Discord refuses any channel beyond 500 — and that refusal hits everyone: the staff, and the bot’s defenses (quarantine channel, channel restored after a deletion). Opening a ticket, joining the on-demand voice hub or asking for a supporter voice channel creates a channel, and each was only limited per member: enough accounts could fill the server. The last 25 slots are now kept for its protection. The refused member is told why, and the owner is warned, once a day.
  • 🔗 A nickname can no longer become a booby-trapped link in the bot’s messages. Discord makes text written as [text](address) clickable, including in the bot’s logs and messages. A member could name themselves — or a thread, their voice channel, their custom role — “Free Nitro” pointing to a phishing site, and the bot displayed it as is, right into the staff logs. These names now show exactly the same, but never again as a hidden link.
  • 📨 The private messages +bug and command suggestions send to the owner are now protected. A member could slip a booby-trapped link into them — in their description, or in a command’s arguments by closing the code block: the bot owner received it clickable, from the bot itself. And nothing capped their number: a single person could send over a thousand a day. Now: at most 5 reports and 5 suggestions per person per day, 20 private messages per hour for the whole bot, and text that shows as is without ever becoming a hidden link. Beyond the hourly budget nothing is lost: the report stays in the server’s log channel.
  • 📩 A banned member can no longer flood the staff with appeals. The “Appeal” button stayed clickable in their private message, after sending as well as after the decision: each appeal went again by private message to the owner and into the log channel, as many times as wanted, with a text that could hide a booby-trapped link. Now, one appeal at a time; after a refusal, the next one is only possible after 7 days — and the banned member is told so, date included. An appeal that couldn’t be delivered to anyone can still be resubmitted.
  • ♻️ +rerank no longer restores roles when it can’t check quarantine. Before giving back removed roles, the command checks that the member is neither quarantined nor barred from roles. If that check failed (database momentarily unavailable), it concluded "neither" and restored the roles — including to a quarantined member, who left quarantine without anyone lifting it. Now, when in doubt, no role is restored and the bot says so.
  • 📭 A custom command set to “DM the target” can no longer rain messages on someone. Set to send a private message to the mentioned member, it let whoever typed it pick the person — staff and owner included — and send it again and again: the command’s cooldown only limited the sender. Now, the same person receives a command’s message at most once every 10 minutes, whoever sends it; anyone who insists is told so.
  • 🖱️ Clicking a security button over and over no longer floods the log channel. Every click on a sensitive button leaves a trace there, even when refused — on purpose, an attempt gets traced. But without any pacing, any member who could see such a button (“Undo” under a ban announced in a public channel, for instance) could click endlessly: one trace per click, with the real alerts stuck behind. Now: one trace per member and per button every 30 seconds, and at most 20 per minute for a server.
  • 🚪 The automatic join role can no longer give access back to someone security is isolating. The bot waits three seconds before giving the join role, to let security act first — and then only checked whether the member already carried the quarantine role. But during a raid, precisely when arrivals are being quarantined, preparing the isolation can take longer than three seconds: the join role landed in that gap, escaped the quarantine clean-up, and since Discord lets one role's permission override another role's denial, it could reopen the very channels the quarantine was closing. The check now reads the actual quarantine list, and if that list cannot be read, the role is simply not given.
  • 🛡️ Three alerts no longer hand the owner the booby-trapped link they report. The “link in the nickname” alert copied the offending nickname — one well-placed character and the link became clickable again, in the owner’s private message. Same for the reason and message of a report, and for the origin server’s name in threat-network alerts. These texts now show exactly the same, without ever becoming a hidden link again.
  • 🛡️ Switching the bot off by unticking its permissions no longer goes unnoticed. The bot already warned owners when an important role was REMOVED from it. But the role that carries its permissions — the one Discord creates on invite — cannot be removed from it: you can only untick its permissions, and that action triggered nothing at all. Yet it is the first move of a compromised admin account before a raid: neutralize the security bot quietly. Now, as soon as one of the bot's roles loses its essential permissions and the bot no longer holds them elsewhere, owners get the critical alert — and if the bot cannot check its own situation, it alerts anyway rather than staying silent.
  • 🛡️ A report's action buttons now judge rank and limits IN the server concerned, not in the one the click came from. Before banning, kicking, muting or warning from a report, the bot checks that the moderator outranks the target, that the target isn't the server owner, and that moderation limits are respected. Those three checks were still made against the server the click came from: from another server, or from a direct message, they no longer protected anything. They now happen where the permission check already happened — in the report's own server.
  • 🚫 The reaction blacklist no longer claims to have removed an emoji that is still there. When someone adds a forbidden reaction, the bot removes it and says so in a short message. But if the removal failed, the message went out anyway — the emoji stayed visible right above a warning saying it was gone. The message is now posted only if the removal actually happened. And when the channel had just been deleted, owners got a "missing Manage Messages permission" alert for a channel that no longer existed: that false alert is gone.
  • 🧾 A message quoted by the bot is no longer a booby-trapped link. In the logs — deleted message (often right after security removed it), edited, purged, a banned member’s last messages, an AutoMod block — as in a suggestion posted with +suggest, a member’s text was copied as is, and a hidden link became clickable again under the bot’s name. The text still shows exactly the same, addresses visible, but never again as a hidden link. Same fix for a scheduled event’s name.
  • 🛡️ A temporary role can no longer be handed to someone barred from receiving roles. +temprole never consulted the +blrank / +bl list: the role was granted, the expiry was recorded, the moderator read "assigned" — and the anti-raid protection then took the role back within a second and raised an alert. The refusal is now immediate, and it says which of the two lists stands in the way. Same command, second fix: if the anti-escalation check cannot run, the role is no longer granted by default — the action is refused as a precaution.
  • 🔒 A quarantine reason can no longer hide a booby-trapped link. It comes from the staff, the automod or the threat network — which writes another server’s name into it, chosen by that server’s owner. Copied as is into the log, the owners’ private message and the isolated member’s, it could carry a hidden link signed by the bot, then re-share it across the network. It now shows exactly the same, without ever becoming a hidden link again.
  • 📋 The post-attack report no longer disappears if the bot restarts during the wave. When an attack subsides, the bot sends the owner a summary — duration, security actions taken, actors, protection grade — and offers to restore a backup from before the damage. The start of the wave was only held in memory: a restart between the start and the return to calm erased everything, so no report and no restore offer. It is precisely the most violent wave that makes a bot restart, so the silence fell at the worst possible moment. The marker is now kept, and the reported duration is that of the attack actually observed — not the downtime.
  • 🔒 The post-attack report can no longer hide a booby-trapped link. It replays incidents exactly as they were recorded, and three of its four columns carry text from elsewhere: a nickname, another server’s name written by the threat network, the action taken. A [text](link) became clickable again in the staff channel, including for incidents recorded weeks ago — fixed at display time, so those are covered too.
  • 🔊 A support voice channel can no longer be deleted with people still in it. To tell whether a voice channel was busy, the bot read its member list — a list that empties itself when the bot frees memory, without anyone having left. A support channel judged empty was then deleted after five minutes… along with its occupants. The same misunderstanding cut voice XP: if just ONE of the two participants vanished from that list, NOBODY received XP or rank minutes. The bot now reads voice states, which never empty — and that reading, which existed only in the on-demand channels feature, is now shared by everyone.
  • 🐞 A report sent with +bug is no longer lost when the bot is updated. The report log and the command-suggestion log were being overwritten with their original version on every update: everything sent since the previous one vanished, at the very moment we came to fix what it contained. They are now kept from one update to the next.
  • 🧪 The automated checks that run before every release now cover two paths they used to skip: messages written inside a ticket, and a quarantined member coming back to the server. Both protections already existed and work — but no check replayed them before a deployment, so a regression there would have gone unnoticed. Also, those checks can no longer make any network call: they were silent by accident, now they are silent by design.
  • 🔒 The bot no longer mass-mentions your server by accident. An @everyone inside text it copies — a question, a name, an answer from elsewhere — could turn into a real mass mention signed by the bot. Its messages now only mention what they explicitly ask for: raid alerts and announcements still wake the right people, everything else just displays. Along the way, "Podium roles enabled" stops pinging the three roles it lists.
  • 🔒 When a quarantined member comes back and the bot cannot re-isolate them, the owners are now told — with the reason. Leaving the server drops the isolation role, and the bot re-applies it on return: a quarantine holds until you decide otherwise. But when it failed — role deleted, setting wiped by a restore, role moved above the bot's, permission removed — the only person informed was the member themselves. The alert now goes to the crown, naming the cause, and the return is recorded in the server log (successful or failed).
  • 🔢 Counter channels work again after a backup. Restoring or loading a backup left the counters (Members, In voice, Boosts…) switched off for good. The two lists that make them work — which channel shows which metric — only make sense read against each other, so the restore dropped both rather than have every counter display its neighbour's value. Nothing said so, and everything had to be ticked again by hand. The bot now recognises each counter by its channel label and reconnects the whole set on its own — including per-role counters, whose role changed id along the way. It creates no channel and deletes none, leaves everything alone if your counters already work, and the report says how many came back and how many were not found.
  • 📄 Loading a backup now lists ALL of its settings. The preview announced “12 setting(s) out of 180 copied” without saying which: there was no way to check before starting that a setting kept for months would travel, nor to understand why the others stay behind. A file is now attached to the preview with the complete list: the settings that are copied, those that stay, and the reason for each. Names only — a setting's value can be a secret (panic word, messages, lists).
  • 🔗 In +createur, a YouTube channel name can no longer hijack its own link. The followed-channels list shows each name as a link to that channel; a name containing the right characters made that link point elsewhere — and the name is whatever the channel owner picks, refreshed automatically. Names now display exactly as they are without ever moving the link, and a very long name no longer makes the whole list disappear.
  • 🧪 The check that replays the bot's buttons "with the wrong hand" now also replays them from inside a server, where clicks actually happen. It only replayed them in direct messages: out of 333 buttons it could only really exercise twelve, the rest answering "this is handled in the server" before any permission check. It now exercises 67, and it states plainly the 115 it still cannot reach — a check that stays silent about what it ignores ends up being trusted wrongly. No flaw found along the way: the five open-to-everyone surfaces it surfaced (daily challenge, support menu, personal alert setting, ticket opening) are public by design, and each is now documented with its reason.
  • 🔇 Server mute and deafen now say WHO, and why. The line existed — “X was muted in #voice” — but it carried neither the author nor the reason, and it could get lost among voice joins and leaves without being archived as evidence. Yet it is the same sanction as a timeout, which has done all three for a long time. The log now names the moderator, shows the reason they wrote, and — when you have set a channel for mutes — files it with the other mutes. It costs nothing on the frequent path: joining or leaving a voice channel queries nothing.
  • 🔇 The anti-spam's automatic mute can no longer fail in silence. If I was missing the “Timeout Members” permission, the anti-spam and mass-mention guards did delete messages and warn — but the mute applied to nobody, and nothing said so: you could believe your spammers were silenced for thirty seconds. You are now told, once, with the action to take. An unexpected refusal from Discord is reported too. A target placed above me stays silent, though: that is Discord's hierarchy, not a failure, and warning you every time would turn the alert into noise.
  • 🎁 The voice-gift announcement names the winner without mentioning them. You asked for it: the nickname only, no ping. The announcement still goes to the text channel of the voice channel the winner is in — they read it where they already are — but it no longer notifies anyone, and a nickname containing “@everyone” stays plain text.
  • 🛡️ A new check now guards the half of the bot's buttons the previous one could not reach. Buttons served by a "collector" (bound to one specific message, like a game or a confirmation) do not go through the usual router: no forged-button test could exercise them. The new check verifies that none of them acts — ban, grant a role, write a setting — without knowing who clicked. Measured: 102 collectors, only one concerned, and it is legitimate (a confirmation sent by direct message to the owner: nobody else can click it). No flaw found; the class is now guarded for future buttons.
  • 🔊 The “In voice” counter no longer forgets anyone, and neither does +vc. To tell who was in a voice channel, the bot read a list that only keeps the people still held in its working memory — which is emptied every hour. The result: three people in voice, two displayed, and nothing to notice it. A channel filled entirely with “forgotten” people even vanished from +vc. Counters and the listing now count everyone. And a report made in voice keeps the COMPLETE list of who was there — the evidence that makes such a report usable.
  • ⭐ The best-of can no longer leak a closed channel's content. Nothing stopped a message written in a ticket, a staff channel or a quarantine — its text and its image — from being republished in plain sight in the best-of channel the whole server reads: all it took was enough stars, and the threshold can be set as low as 1. The bot now only republishes what @everyone could already read, judging a thread by the channel that contains it. On any doubt it abstains — and it does not mark the message as “already posted”, so a later star can still publish it if the channel opens up.
  • 🧪 A development copy of the bot can no longer touch your servers. The bot already knows to stand down when it runs as a test copy — but three modules escaped that rule, and one acted on every start-up: the on-demand voice channels feature, which deletes empty temporary channels. A test copy running on the same account was therefore cleaning up real channels. The other two rewrote every server's configuration (mass hardening) and their protection grade. All three now stand down like their twelve neighbours, and the guard names what it holds back.
  • 🛡️ Mass hardening no longer claims success when it failed. It marked its version as “applied” even when some servers could not be hardened — and that marking blocks any retry: a server left unprotected stayed that way forever, the only trace being a technical log line. The version is now marked only if every server went through; otherwise the next start-up retries, which costs nothing to those already hardened.
  • ⏳ A temporary role can no longer become permanent by accident. When the bot cannot save a temporary role's end date — bought in the shop or granted by staff — it now cancels cleanly: the role is taken back, and in the shop nothing is charged. Previously the role stayed on the member with no deadline at all, and the announced date existed nowhere.
  • 🚨 If your panic word stays on screen, you find out right away. When you type the secret word, the bot deletes your message to hide it — but if it can't (missing “Manage Messages” in that channel), the word stayed in plain sight and nothing told you. You now get a critical alert naming the channel and telling you what to do. It does not repeat the word, of course. And it fires even if the server was already locked down — which was precisely the case where you learned nothing.
  • ♻️ +rerank can now repair a demotion with no deadline — +rerank fenetre illimite. Until now the repair window was 24 h by default and 30 days at most: past that, roles removed by a protection could no longer be restored by the command, and had to be put back by hand. The word illimite (or unlimited) makes it so a derank no longer expires. ⚠️ That does not mean "endless archive": the server still keeps at most 50 deranks at a time, the most recent ones — beyond that the oldest drop out, and every screen announcing the unlimited window says so. It applies from now on: what had already dropped out of memory does not come back. You can go back to a finite window whenever you want (+rerank fenetre 48h), and the setting also lives in +menu → Advanced settings. When the derank is more than 30 days old, the confirmation screen says so: a role may have been edited since, and it is its current permissions that will be given back. The checks themselves have not moved an inch: owner only, confirmation required, refusal for a member in quarantine or barred from roles. A longer window is not a wider permission.
  • 🎭 +addrole now accepts the role NAME, in whatever order you like. As requested: +addrole protect @member grants @Protect, with no mention and no ID to copy — and the member can come before or after the role. Accents, case and emojis in the name are ignored (“moderateur” finds @Modérateur, “vip” finds @⭐ VIP). Both older forms work exactly as before. What the near match will never do, since you also asked for this to be safe: it will not grant a role carrying sensitive permissions (Administrator, Manage Roles, Ban…) on an approximation — those need the exact name, a mention or an ID, and the refusal says which role and why. If several roles look alike, the bot does not pick: it lists them and lets you decide. If two roles become identical once emojis and look-alike characters are stripped — the old trick of a fake “Protect” sitting next to the real one — it refuses too. @everyone is never reachable by name. And the member must still be pointed at: replying to someone does not turn them into the target. Every usual check (rank blacklist, privilege-escalation guard, hierarchy, protected target) applies to a role found by name exactly as it does to a mentioned role, and the security log records the text that found it.
  • 🧹 After a raid, the restore report can no longer state a number it does not know. When the bot cannot save the cleanup of its own channels, it now SAYS so in the report, and the security log writes "?" instead of "0". Previously the durable record claimed "0 channels removed" while some may in fact have been deleted — in the very document you reread to understand what happened.
  • 🇫🇷 A French security alert no longer contains English. When someone grants themselves sensitive permissions, the alert you receive showed an “↩️ Auto-revert” field — the only English one among “Recommended resolution” and “Decision”, and right above a line reading “Revert failed”. The French wording now matches the rest. (English is unchanged.)
  • 🥇 Cutting the podium roles can no longer make the bot forget roles it did not delete. When a role sits higher than the bot's own, Discord refuses to delete it: the bot now SAYS so in its reply, and keeps track of the role so you can retry after moving its own role up. Previously the role stayed on the server — hoisted, orphaned — while the bot forgot its id, leaving no way to remove it, with "0 roles deleted" inside a success message as the only clue.
  • 🛡️ The security panel can no longer go stale in silence. When the bot cannot save the id of the panel it just posted, it now SAYS so in its errors — and more importantly the panel stays registered, so it keeps updating. Previously the failure went out without a word and skipped registration: the panel existed, looked alive, and never refreshed again.
  • 🔒 An unreadable quarantine state no longer reads as “nobody is in quarantine”. When the list of isolated members cannot be read back — a truncated write, a momentarily locked database — the bot used to answer “there is nobody”, and rewards went out again. It now answers “I don’t know”, and holds instead of granting: a missed role can be handed out by hand, while an access given back to someone just isolated undoes the quarantine. Three places benefit. +rerank refuses and says so (it used to hand roles back to an isolated member with nothing shown); the autorole is no longer granted to a newcomer while we cannot tell who is isolated; and +booster sync skips quarantined members and SAYS SO, with its own line in the report — role removal still happens in every case, because not being able to read is no reason to leave a reward with someone who no longer qualifies.
  • 🔒 Guardian audit's "Quarantine" button can no longer confirm an isolation that did not happen. It now reads the verdict: when the quarantine role could not be applied, staff read "they are NOT isolated — they can still post everywhere, move my role higher" instead of "quarantined (permissions removed)". Previously the confirmation went out whatever the outcome — so staff stopped watching a still-active member, believing they had neutralised them.
  • 🥇 Two podium-role save failures no longer go out in silence. When the bot cleans up duplicate roles, or remembers the leaderboard it has just posted, a write failure was swallowed without a word — the configuration could then name a deleted role, or the board was never refreshed again. Both now SAY so in the error log. The deleted roles and the posted board stay in place: only the bookkeeping was missing, and that is what gets named.
  • 🧾 The command log no longer renders a booby-trapped link. A command's parameters are shown there inside a code block. A single backtick typed in the command closed that block, and what followed could turn into a masked link (clickable text whose destination you can't see) in the staff channel, under the bot's name. Any member could do it with a public command. Typed backticks now show as « ʻ », and everything else stays readable character for character, including when the backtick comes from a nickname.
  • 🔊 Voice XP: bots no longer count towards “at least two”. Since late September, a member alone with a music bot earned their voice XP and auto-rank minutes as if there were two of them. That is exactly the “stay alone all night” the rule was meant to block. It now takes two people who are not bots again. Anyone who used to sit alone with a bot will notice, and that is intended. Nothing changes with two or more humans.
  • 🧾 Restoring a backup no longer rewinds +rerank's memory. +backup restore used to rewrite the history of removed roles as it was when the backup was taken. Deranks that happened after the backup vanished, often those of the very incident that prompted the restore. And roles already given back showed up again as "to restore". The history is now treated as live state, like ongoing quarantines: a restore — including the one offered after a raid — leaves it as it is. The +rerank window is a setting and is still restored.
  • 📋 The quarantine can no longer become a logs channel, neither through +setlogs nor through its routing. The +setup panel already refused a channel the bot uses for something else (quarantine, reports…). +setlogs accepted it. It now refuses it, along with any thread opened in such a channel. Routing (+setlogs routes) refuses it too: sending bans to the quarantine would have handed them to the very members just isolated there. For the logs and changelog channels, the +setup panel also refuses a channel that doesn't belong to this server instead of saving it. Routing now refuses any channel the bot already uses (for instance surprise crates to #games); routes already saved keep working. Finally, the bot's update announcement can no longer land in the reports or quarantine channel.
  • 🖼️ +banner (alias +bannière) — shows a member's profile banner in full size (the one on their Discord account, not a server-specific profile). Mention them, paste their ID, reply to their message, or leave it empty for your own. Without a banner, the bot shows the profile colour (#000000 included) or says there is none. If Discord doesn't answer, it says it can't check, never "no banner" instead. Until now, +banner answered "Did you mean +ban?".
  • 🌐 +addrole moderateur <member> now finds “Moderator”. A role can have an English name while you type it in French, or the other way round. “moderateur” did not find “Moderator | ⭐ |”, because only the end of the word differs. +addrole now recognises the French/English equivalent of a role name (modérateur/moderator, animateur/animator, créateur/creator…). It compares the whole name, and only when nothing else matches. Since it is a guessed translation, the bot first shows the role it found and the member. It only gives the role after a click from the command's author, within 30 seconds, and everything is checked again at the moment of the click. A role with sensitive permissions is never given this way (a moderation role that can kick, ban or time out members is one): only its exact name, its mention or its ID can point to it. Every outcome (given, cancelled, expired, denied) is written to the security log.
  • 🏆 Champion of the month: one role, and no more lifetime medal. Two bugs made the role show up “twice”. On the 1st of the month, the games rotation and the activity podium run at the same time. On a server that did not have the role yet, each could create its own. The extra one stayed: empty, or worn by the games champion with no rotation ever taking it back. They now create only one. Second bug: when reward roles are disabled, a former activity champion kept “🏆 Champion of the month” month after month, next to each new games champion. Now the activity title no longer counts in that case. The former champion loses the role at the next rotation, and the log channel says who and why. With reward roles enabled, nothing changes: the games winner and the activity winner can still both hold it. A role that was already duplicated is not deleted automatically yet.
  • 📦 The log finally follows channel moves. Dragging a channel, moving it to another category or reorganising a whole category left no trace, or just a bare “Category changed” without saying which one. Each gesture now produces a single “📦 Channel moved” message that states what is true: “#channel: position 5 → 2 — category Projects”, or “category Projects → Archives”. Neighbours that Discord renumbers along the way are never accused of having moved, and forty channels reordered at once fit in one message. Deleting a category gives one line per channel in that same message, instead of one “Channel updated” each. The author is named only when Discord's audit log proves it; otherwise “Unknown”, with the reason. Channels excluded with +antiupdate ignore stay silent, as do moves that the audit log attributes to the bot itself. 🔧 “Channel updated” now says everything that changed. On top of the name, slow mode and NSFW: the topic, before and after (except for a private channel, whose text is never copied into the log channel), the type (text ↔ announcement), a voice channel's bitrate, user limit, region and video quality, thread auto-archive and thread slow mode, and for a forum its tags, default reaction, sort order, layout and required tag. Settings of a temporary voice channel, which its owner changes from their panel, stay silent. A change is no longer attributed to the author of another change made to the same channel just before. Channel creation and deletion logs now show the category and the type. Permissions that grant no power stay silent, as before: quarantine and lockdown still produce nothing.
  • ⛔ A refused command now leaves a trace in the log channel. When a member types a command they have no access to (+ban, +addrole, a command reserved for the owner…), the bot answers them as before. The log channel now also gets a "⛔ Command refused" entry. It shows who typed the command, which one, against which target, and what blocked it (for a missing permission: required tier and held tier). It also shows their highest role, their account age and a link to the message. As with buttons, a burst does not flood the channel: at most one trace per member and per command every 30 seconds, and twenty per minute for the server. The next trace from the same member for the same command says how many of their attempts were not logged. These traces are written even when the full command audit is turned off, and they never count toward its automatic shutoff. A command that crashes also leaves a "💥 Command failed" entry, which gives the type of error but never its details. Finally, when a command answers with a red message, such as a refusal (hierarchy, target not found…), its log entry also turns red and repeats the reply shown: a refused +ban no longer reads like an executed +ban.
  • 🧹 +nuke in the log channel created a second 📋-logs. While the command recreated the wiped channel, the automatic log-channel rebuild made another one. The log went there, and the channel you had just wiped was left behind, duplicated. Same when the log channel was deleted by hand with anti-delete on: two channels instead of one. A deleted channel now has a single recreator. The settings that named the old channel (log channel, welcome, announcements, levels…) follow the recreated channel, even with anti-delete off. Settings that list several channels do not follow (a log type's own channel in +setlogs, drop channels…): check them again when a channel is recreated. +nuke says so in its confirmation.
  • 🔗 Your log channel stays the one you picked. If you had picked an announcement channel, a thread or a voice channel's text chat, my duplicate scanner did not recognise it. It assumed the setting was empty and silently pointed it back to your old 📋-logs, so your logs went back to the channel you had just left. I no longer replace a channel I can see. Your original 📋-logs stays where it is: I tell you about it once and leave it alone. If I can no longer find the saved channel (deleted, or an archived thread), I link the setting to the only remaining one and I tell you, naming the old and the new. The same goes for the quarantine, report and verification channels.
  • 🎭 +massrole no longer hands out a role with sensitive permissions (administration, managing the server, roles, channels or webhooks, ban, kick, timeout, nicknames, @everyone) in bulk, for anyone, server owner included. The refusal says so and points to +addrole, one member at a time. Removing such a role in bulk still works. A mass operation now applies exactly the confirmed selection, even if another panel is used while it runs, and refuses any action other than Add, Remove or Replace.
  • 👥 +memberlist: every member of the server in a single embed, page by page (⏮ ◀ ▶ ⏭, or +memberlist 12 to jump straight to a page). For each one: username, ID and join date, oldest first. If Discord does not send the whole list, or the total member count, the command says so instead of showing a wrong total. Moderators only, like +lastseen (aliases +members, +membres) — but the list is posted in the channel where the command is typed, readable by everyone who can see it: run it in a staff channel.
  • 📌 Pins from a channel @everyone can't see (or from a private thread) are no longer copied into the pin log, even a staff-only one: they are announced in their own channel, and +pinlog says so. On a verification server, where a role rather than @everyone opens the channels, the pin log therefore no longer receives pins from those channels. The best-of, for its part, no longer reposts a message from a private thread. +pinlog salon refuses the quarantine and the bot's other channels. A custom command's log does the same, through +custom as well as +setup. A destination or log already set to one of those channels is no longer used: another one has to be picked (+pinlog points it out).
  • 🧭 +setup panel: a channel from THIS server, or nothing. When the panel was opened outside its own server, it accepted a channel from another server for welcome, goodbye, ghost ping, verification, level announcements, starboard, suggestions, the role menu and custom commands. The setting showed up, but nothing was ever sent there. These pickers now refuse such a channel, say so, and save nothing, as the log channel picker already did. A setting already saved this way is not repaired automatically: if it doesn't work, pick the channel again with the panel opened on the server concerned.
  • 🧾 The refused-command log now says "unknown" when it does not know. When the bot did not have the member at hand, the "⛔ Command refused" entry showed "held: 0" and "Highest role: (none)". It now says "(unknown)". A command that answers in red after running is no longer labelled "Error reply", because red does not say whether it failed (+baninfo on a banned member, +safe on a dangerous link answer in red and succeeded). Its field becomes "Red reply shown to the author", including when it declined to act (for example a +ban blocked by the role hierarchy); only the "⛔ Command refused" entry keeps "Error reply". When the same command is run again with the same arguments and answers in green this time, it no longer replaces the red entry: it creates a new entry. The "💥 Command failed" entry no longer links to the command message when the bot deletes it after the error. Finally, when a trace could not be posted (the bot can no longer write in the log channel), the attempts it was meant to report are no longer lost: the next trace for that member and command counts them, including the one that did not go out.
  • 🌑 A custom command eclipsed by a new bot command is now reported. When the bot gains a command (+banner, for instance), a custom command that already used that word, or one of its shortcuts, stopped answering without warning: the bot answered in its place. At startup, the bot now finds each such custom command and says so once in the log channel. The message gives the word, the bot command that answers instead, and how to recreate the custom command under another name. Nothing is deleted or renamed automatically. +custom list also marks these commands with a 🌑. Without a log channel, nothing is posted.
  • 🔊 Voice XP: screen sharing with at least one other member who can hear now doubles that minute's XP (×2). A muted mic, whether muted by the member or by a moderator, earns about 30% less. Deafened members still earn nothing. Both effects stack (×2 × 0.7). A deafened account no longer counts toward the two people required, so being alone with someone who is deafened no longer earns voice XP. +voicexp now shows these rules.
  • Whitelisting someone no longer lifts their blacklist: that takes +unbl, which requires the agreement of two of the server's owners (just one if it only has one). +wl (command or panel) and the audit's "Apply" button explain this when they leave a blacklisted member out. When +unbl also lifts the blacklist on your other servers, it now requires the agreement of each server's owners. Where that agreement is missing, the blacklist stays and the reply says so. Restoring a backup or re-inviting the bot no longer removes anyone from the blacklist: the current list is kept, and the backup's list is added to it.
  • 📰 +news finally shows the latest changes first. A version left open for weeks only listed its ten oldest notes there, under the date it was first published. The most recent now come first. When the date of the latest update is known, it is shown too: “since … · updated …”, or “on …” when everything went out the same day.
  • 🕵️ In the log channel, a change to a role, the server, a thread, a sticker, an emoji or an event is no longer credited to whoever changed another setting. If two moderators touched the same item a few seconds apart, the log could name whoever had acted just before on another setting. In the role permissions log, a mere rename was enough for its author to be named in place of whoever had granted a dangerous permission. These logs are now signed only by the audit log entry that changed that very field. This applies to the name, colour, permissions, owner, vanity URL, verification level, AFK channel, a thread's lock, a sticker's description or an event's date. Otherwise, the log shows “Unknown”, with the reason. And a rename made by the bot no longer makes a moderator's thread lock vanish from the log. 📦 Channel moves are no longer lost. A channel dragged just before the bot restarts is kept in the archive (+logs), with “Unknown” as the author: the bot stopped before it could read the audit log. As with any other move, nothing is kept if the server has no log channel or has turned off the “Channels” type. After a +reset, a move made before the reset no longer shows up in the new log channel. Finally, the daily digest and the end-of-day summary count every move on a single line, “📦 Channel moved”. Before, there were two or three, depending on the number of channels and the server's language. The summary of the day in progress when the update lands may still show the old line.
  • 🎭 +addrole, confirming a role found through its French/English equivalent. If your member record dropped out of the bot's memory during the 30-second confirmation, your click ended in a generic "❌ Execution error", and the log channel only kept a "💥 Command failed" entry, which gives the type of error but not its reason. The bot now re-reads you when you click. If you are still on the server, your click goes through as usual. If it can no longer find you, it refuses and says why, and the log channel records that refusal along with the original proposal. An attempt on the server owner or on the bot keeps its usual refusal and alert. A role whose permissions change while the bot re-reads the members is now caught as well: nothing is given. Finally, the "you no longer have access" refusal names the command with YOUR server's prefix instead of a hard-coded "+addrole", in French and in English.
  • 📊 “Deploy” finally applies your counter selection, and the menu no longer destroys anything on its own. When counters were already in place, picking in +setup → Counters changed them on the spot and mixed the old and new lists. An “In voice” channel got renamed “Online”, the real “Online” channel was deleted, an added counter was never created, and “Deploy” then did nothing at all. The menu now keeps your selection and shows what will change (“⏳ Pending: ➕ / ➖”). When you hit Deploy: - unchecked counters go; - new ones are created; - the ones you keep stay on their channel; - the panel tells you what was done, including when Discord refuses a creation or a deletion, or when another operation is already running. Until your selection is fully in place, it is kept and the panel says so. Another click tries again, even for a counter deleted by hand that Discord had refused to recreate. If a log channel is set, it keeps a record of these actions: a line in your name when you change the selection, and, when you hit Deploy or Remove, a line in your name that names the channels created and deleted. A click that changes nothing leaves none. The setup assistant and +setstats <types> start from that same selection, so what they add is no longer undone by the next “Deploy”. +setstats without arguments also starts from the pending selection, but without role counters, which this command cannot handle: the ones in place are then removed, so use the button for those. +setstats now reports refusals, and +setstats off no longer answers “deleted” while a deployment is running. A channel that the bot re-links by its name alone during a restore (from this version on) is no longer deleted when you uncheck it, unless the bot can prove it created that channel itself: it is left alone and reported. A restored backup or an imported configuration no longer brings a pending selection from another time or another server.
  • ♻️ +rerank no longer forgets. By default, a derank stays repairable with no time limit: it survives a restart and a +reset (its closing message says so), and it only leaves memory once you confirm its repair. The 50-derank-per-server cap is gone: memory now holds up to 10,000, and this safety cap never erases anything. If it is reached, the bot says so: an alert to the owners, a line at the top of +rerank, and +derank states that this derank could not be remembered. You can still set a limit with +rerank fenetre 48h: old deranks are then no longer offered, but they stay in memory, and +rerank fenetre illimite makes them repairable again. If the memory cannot be read, +rerank says so instead of answering "no derank". Without a window setting, deranks older than 24 h that were still in memory become repairable again; anything that had already left memory before this version does not come back.
  • 🌑 The +setup → Custom commands panel now flags eclipsed commands too. A custom command that a bot command now answers in its place is marked with a 🌑 there, as in +custom list. The panel also shows which bot command answers, and how to recreate yours under another name. And if the bot cannot read a server's configuration at startup, the log channel warning is no longer lost: it is retried at the next startup.
  • 🛒 A shop purchase refused at the last moment no longer leaves a trace. The shop re-reads your aura just before charging you: if it melted away in the meantime — a heist, a casino bet, a race started while the bot was talking to Discord — the purchase is refused and nothing is charged. What had already been applied, however, was not undone properly. Re-buying the colour you were already wearing left you with no colour at all, for nothing. The other way round, the custom-role touch-up and the role icon give that role back to you when it had been taken away, and a refused purchase then left it acquired without paying. (If you have the level 50 reward you can also get it back for free that way — so it was not, as first stated here, your only way back.) All three items now restore exactly the state from before, and never take back a role you owned before buying. Two neighbouring cases are covered too: if the role cannot be given back to you, the touch-up already applied is reverted instead of being a gift; and if the icon fails after the role is given back, that is undone as well.
  • 🔒 +massrole, +addrole and +delrole no longer take anyone out of quarantine. +massrole refuses to remove or replace the quarantine role, and no longer gives any other role to quarantined members: each member is checked when their turn comes, and the summary shows how many were left out. +delrole refuses to remove the quarantine role, and +addrole no longer gives any other role to a quarantined member, including on the confirmation click. A quarantine still only ends when it is lifted in +quarantine, with the owners' vote. If the quarantine can't be read, +massrole and +addrole give no other role, and say so.
  • 🎨 The level 50 custom role now tells the truth, and no longer duplicates itself. The same custom role can be obtained two ways: from the shop, or for free at the level 50 reward. The paid door had been hardened three times; the free one, never. From now on: if Discord refuses your change, you are told, instead of being shown a new name and colour on a role that did not change; if your custom role has moved above the bot in the role list, you are told that too instead of quietly getting a second one — the old one then stayed on the server forever, outside any management, and was not even deleted when you left; and the button opens again for everyone, where on some roles it had stopped responding altogether, because the bot was reading a colour Discord no longer sends it.
  • 🔇 +unmute says what it actually lifted. A member who was neither timed out nor voice-muted still got « 🔊 Member unmuted », although nothing had been done: the bot now replies that there was nothing to lift. If the voice mute can’t be removed (missing « Mute Members » permission), it says so — and tells you when the timeout itself was lifted. The « ↩️ Cancel » button on a mute now follows the same hierarchy rule as the command: you can no longer unmute, in one click, someone whose role is equal to or higher than yours. Finally, when the command is typed as a reply to a message, the suggested example uses the server’s prefix.
  • 🪪 You can now see YOUR own permissions on the bot. In the panel, a “My permissions” card lists the commands you can use on this server — computed for you, and visible to you alone: it is never posted in the channel. An administrator sees everything they can do, a member sees what is open to them, and the server owner sees the whole set. No more guessing whether a command will answer “you lack permission”.
  • 🛡️ Podium and champion roles are no longer handed out when they grant permissions. “🏆 Champion of the month”, the games podium roles (“🥇 Top 1 Jeux”…), the 🥈 and 🥉 activity podium roles and “🏆 League Champion” are given automatically by the bot, without anyone asking. If someone added permissions to one of them, the bot then handed those permissions out itself. Now only the permissions that @everyone does not already have count: a role that grants nothing more than the whole server has is still handed out. When the bot knows it created the role itself (always for the champion of the month, the activity podium and the League champion; for the games podium, if it created the role from this version on) and those extra permissions are all among the ones Discord gives @everyone by default, it removes them from the role, only once, says so in the log channel with the list of removed permissions, and keeps handing the role out. This is the case of a role created before the end of August when @everyone has been restricted since: “Mention @everyone” removed, but also, for instance, “View Channels” removed for a join verification — the bot then removes those permissions from the role. If they come back to it later, or if the role's permissions are locked (+lockrole), the bot leaves it alone: the role is suspended. If it cannot read the role again right before touching it, it does not touch it either, does not hand it out on that pass, and says so. A suspended role, like any role that grants another permission @everyone does not have, is neither given nor removed by the bot anymore, no other role is created in its place, and the log channel says so once, with the reason (on a server without a log channel, as soon as it has one). ⚠️ This is intended: a permission that @everyone does not have, added by hand, even a harmless one (“Manage Messages”…), suspends the role until it is removed from it, and whoever wears the role keeps it. The games podium duplicate clean-up no longer deletes a role on its name alone, and enabling the games podium roles no longer takes over an existing role on its name alone: when an existing role stops it from finishing, it says which one and why. Finally, the public activity podium announcement no longer says “the 🥇🥈🥉 roles are theirs” when one of them was not handed out.
  • 🔒 The quarantine's isolation role can no longer be used as an automatic role: boost role, birthday role, auto-role, verification role, level reward, +autorank tier, supporter role, custom-command role, role for sale or rent, role-menu entry — every setting (command, +setup panel, assistant) refuses it and explains why. No automatic module gives it to or removes it from a member anymore, even if it had been set before this update, and +derank, +bl and automatic sanctions leave it in place. If the verification role is the isolation role, verification is suspended and the owners are notified. 🎂🚀 The birthday-role cleanup, +booster sync and the end of a boost now only take a role back from members the bot gave it to: for a role set after this update, a role held for another reason (staff, given by hand) is not removed. For a role set before, the bot treats as having received it from the bot the members celebrated the day before or that same day (birthday) and those who are boosting (booster); everyone else keeps it. +booster sync counts the holders it kept because their origin is unknown. +birthday role also refuses a role with sensitive permissions.
  • 🔒 A quarantined member stays isolated even if someone removes the isolation role by hand: the bot puts it back as soon as it sees the removal, and warns the owners (log channel and DM, grouped), naming the author when Discord's audit log identifies them. If a release voted in +quarantine could not remove the role, removing it by hand afterwards is still accepted for 90 days — except after a server +reset, or if its configuration is damaged: then vote again. Giving the isolation role or the verification role to a blacklisted member is no longer treated as a forbidden role: no “role removed” antiraid alert, and no sanction for whoever gave it. The only way out is still the 🔓 Release button, confirmed by the owners.
  • 🔒 The +oncall off, +digest off, +setlogs audit off and +setverify challenge off commands are now reserved to the server owner and their owners. Administrators can still turn these protections on.
  • 🛡️ Turning a protection back on cancels its pending disabling. When disabling a critical protection is waiting for a second owner's validation and you turn it back on in the meantime — with its command (+antiban on, +antibot on, +antiraid all on, +automod antilink on…), with the setup assistant, with hardening or from a panel —, the request is withdrawn: the second owner can no longer turn it off. Module commands say so in their reply, or say that the request could not be withdrawn, or that they could not check it.
  • 🔒 Tickets and quarantine. A quarantined member no longer gets into a ticket through the bot: they can't open one, be added to one with +add or through a transfer, or bring someone into their own. The refusal says so, and their way to appeal remains the quarantine channel. The isolation role is no longer accepted as the ticket team: +ticket role and the settings screen refuse it, a staff role already set to it is ignored (tickets then show as “not configured”), and a ticket type's access roles leave it out. When the bot can't read the quarantine, it holds back and says so.
  • 🔒 +autolock, +autounlock, +autohide and +autounhide now respect channel access. These four commands now require Discord's “Manage Roles” permission instead of “Manage Channels”: it is the one Discord requires to edit a channel's permissions. Roles you gave the moderation tier with +perm keep them. They refuse a channel you can't see, and that also applies to cancelling its automatic return, with cancel as with cancel all. When a channel is only open for a while, what counts is the state it will return to. Finally, restarting a temporary lock or hide that is already running now only moves the return time: at the end, the channel gets back the state it had before the first command, and the summary says so.
  • 🛡️ The “Discord AutoMod rule neutralised” and “burst deletion of emojis or stickers” alerts now fire: the bot read the wrong field of Discord’s audit log, so neither alert ever triggered. Disabling or deleting an AutoMod rule now notifies the server owners by DM, with a ping; so does deleting 5 emojis or stickers in under a minute, with at most one warning per burst, naming whoever deleted them. Outside reinforced monitoring, the server owner’s own actions do not trigger these alerts: they stay logged in the log channel, with their name. None of these actions counts towards the reputation shared between servers.
  • 🛒 The shop no longer hands out a role that grants power. What it already refused, it still refuses: listing or selling a role with sensitive permissions, or the quarantine isolation role. It now also refuses, when listing (+shop addrole, +shop addtemprole) as when buying a permanent or rented role — even one already listed —, a role that carries a +perm tier, opens bot commands (+cmdperm, +permsalon, the allowed role of a +custom command), is named in a team or security setting (ticket staff, reports, alert roles, verification), or grants, on the role or through a channel override, a moderation or management permission (manage messages, threads or events, mute or deafen in voice, move members, pin messages, bypass slowmode, view audit log…). The color item, when it reuses a color that already exists, and the custom-role icon, when it gives that role back to a member who no longer holds it, now apply all these refusals, sensitive permissions and the isolation role included. The custom-role edit and the level 50 custom-role button, when they give the role back, apply them too: a custom role that carries one of these permissions is no longer cleaned and given back, it is refused. When refused, nothing is charged and the role is neither given nor changed; the reason is shown to the staff member listing it.
  • 🛡️ A custom command that bans, kicks or mutes now goes through the same safeguards as +ban: it uses up the +modlimit limit of its sanction (ban, kick or tempsmute) and counts, like +ban and in the same counter, toward protection against bursts of destructive actions. A corrected typo uses up the limit of the command it runs. +modlimit add saves the rule under the name of the command the bot actually runs (tempmute becomes tempsmute) and refuses, saying so, a name that is not a bot command or that is a custom command’s keyword; +modlimit flags a rule set on a name that is not a bot command, or on +modlimit itself.
  • 🔒 Safer emergency lockdown (+lockdown, +panic, the +base panel, the panic word): the bot saves every channel’s state BEFORE closing the first one — a restart in the middle of a lockdown no longer leaves the server closed with no way to reopen it. If it cannot save that state, it closes nothing and says so, instead of announcing a lockdown that did not happen or stopping without a word; the panic word alert then also says where the verification level stands. If, when reopening, it cannot clear that state, it says so on every way out (+lockdown off, +panic off, “Re-enable everything”, the confirmation button and +lockword approve) and explains what to do.
  • 🔒 A member in quarantine no longer receives any role from the bot outside of the lift. Levelling up, the level-reward catch-up, the boost role, the activity rank, the birthday role, the supporter role, role menus, the shop (role, rental, nickname color, icon, custom role — nothing is charged), verification, +joueur, the level 50 custom role and the +bug reward no longer give them anything until their quarantine is lifted: a role received while isolated reopened channels to them, and survived the lift. +temprole refuses too, and +addrole, +massrole and +booster sync now refuse from the very start of the quarantine. A Guardian "Allow" and +undo no longer give their other roles back: they are kept in +rerank, and this is said; +rerank checks the quarantine again after the click. The quarantine role is always given, and as soon as the owners have voted the lift, the member is served again. What the isolation refused them — a level reward reached, the boost role of a boost started, the auto-role of an arrival — is named at the lift, in the log channel and in the report, with the command to give it back; the +levelrole add summary also names the quarantined members it skipped.
  • 🕵️ Security alerts name the right person. Permission escalation alerts, the server ownership transfer alert and the locked role alert name whoever made that very change, no longer whoever had just touched another role or another setting a few seconds earlier. When Discord's audit log is slow to fill in, they wait for the entry, a few seconds at most; if it cannot establish the author, they say “author not found” and explain why. Same rule for the “Trust but verify” alert and the promotion series: they only name whoever actually gave the role. And a change made by the bot or by the owner on another role no longer silences someone else's escalation alert, nor makes it less urgent. A moved locked role says right away that no one can be named: Discord does not record that change in the audit log. 🛡️ Protections target the real author, and reverting does not wait. When a role, the server or a member's roles are changed, the anti-raid only sanctions, Guardian only puts under watch, and the danger index only counts the person who actually made that change, including during a burst of changes. Dangerous permissions added to a role are removed right away, without waiting for the author to be known — by Guardian, and by the anti-raid for Administrator, for @everyone or when its anti-permissions mode is on; with anti-permissions on, a dangerous role given to a member is taken back right away too. What the bot restores itself (role lock, restore, quarantine release, +rerank, +recover) is never removed, and no longer raises an alert. A change made just before by the bot or by a trusted account on the same role no longer makes someone else's escalation look legitimate — even when it had granted exactly the same permissions before they were removed. A change made with the bot's token by another program is reverted, and the alert says so. When the bot cannot reliably order these changes in time, it reverts as a precaution and says “author not found” rather than naming the wrong person — including right after a restart or a reconnection, when it could not see the previous changes. If the author then turns out to be a trusted account or the owner, the alert names them and says the removal was a precaution, so they can do it again. Without the “View Audit Log” permission, the bot cannot name anyone: it then removes those permissions whoever the author is, owner included, and the alert says which permission it is missing. Reordering roles or receiving a boost no longer counts against anyone.
  • ✏️ +nick — a moderator, or an administrator who is not an owner of the server, can no longer have the bot rename a member whose role is equal to or higher than their own: that is the rule Discord enforces directly. Renaming yourself still works. When replying to a message, +nick now targets the member written in the command, by mention or by ID (the help says so: @member/ID), instead of the person being replied to. Typed with no target in a reply, +nick (or +nick forget) says so instead of guessing.
  • 🔐 +customperm finally applies to commands open to everyone. Raising a public command (+customperm snipe admin, or +customperm all public admin) now really restricts it to the chosen tier — until now, the ✅ reply had no effect on them. +editsnipe now follows the tier of +snipe. +joueur, +birthday, +report and +help stay open to everyone: +customperm says so instead of pretending to close them. If your server had raised public commands before this update, they are now restricted, and your log channel, if it has one, receives the list.
  • 🔒 A damaged command or role tier can no longer open anything. An unreadable command tier (after loading a permission preset, an old backup or a manual edit of the database) now closes the command instead of opening it to everyone, and an unreadable role tier no longer grants anything. +customperm list flags unreadable command tiers so you can fix them.
  • 🔀 +moveall no longer turns a targeted move into moving everyone in voice. An argument it did not recognise — a member who left the server, a text channel, a channel name with spaces, a wrong ID — was ignored without a word: if you were in voice, +moveall @member-who-left then moved everyone in the server's voice channels to yours, and +moveall #channel #typo poured everyone into the first channel. It now refuses, moves no one and names the argument at fault; an extra word after a correct move is refused too. +moveall alone still moves everyone to your voice channel.
  • Beyond five ticket types, no ticket could be opened at all. Past that count the panel swaps its buttons for a dropdown, and clicking that dropdown answered nothing: "This interaction failed", no channel created, nothing in the logs. The dropdown now goes through the same opening gate as the buttons — and therefore through the same checks: blocklist, quarantine, required role, cooldown between tickets, and the cap on open tickets.
  • 🔒 When their quarantine is lifted by vote, a member now receives what the isolation refused them, and +undo no longer puts back into quarantine a member the vote released. A level reward reached, a new grade (the old one is removed, as on a level-up), the boost role of a boost started, the auto-role of an arrival during the isolation: the lift now gives them, and says so in the log channel and in the report. A role the team had removed before the quarantine is not given back (leaving and coming back erases that removal: the auto-role of a return is given). A lift interrupted then replayed only catches up on what the isolation refused up to the first decision, and does not give a second time what the first one had given and recorded. What cannot be given with certainty or without risk — arrival just before the isolation, sensitive permissions, a new isolation during the lift — is named, with the command to use; when the lift cannot judge it or give it — unknown start, unreadable data, rank block —, it says so, with the reason. The isolation role the attacker removed from a member the vote released after the attack is given back neither by +undo nor by the confirmed recovery: their other roles are, and this is said; when the lift record or the quarantine state is unreadable, the role is given back, and this is said too. A new quarantine started during a lift keeps its saved roles and its isolation role: what the lift had just given back or given is removed and kept until its own lift, and this is said at the top of the report. A member released by the vote whose lift was interrupted is no longer put back into quarantine when they come back, and releasing a member while they are being quarantined now reports, in the log channel, the roles that did not come back.
  • 🛒 Custom role: a name, not an ad The custom role (shop and level 50) refuses a link (https://…), an invite (dsc.gg/…), a .com or .fr site, or a .gg or .me address followed by a path (t.me/…). If refused, nothing is charged.
  • 🔒 cancel all on automatic locks and hides: owners only cancel all of +autolock, +autohide, +autounlock and +autounhide: owners only. cancel #channel stays open to moderators, channel by channel.
  • 🧾 Command audit: temporary pause, your setting stays intact Under heavy load, the audit pauses for up to an hour, then resumes on its own without touching +setlogs audit. Each pause is announced in the logs channel, with the resume time and the main sources.
  • 🔫 The BANG duel GIF is set with “Manage Server” +bang gif <url> requires the Manage Server permission. An address the bot cannot display, or longer than 400 characters, is refused; an unreadable saved image gives way to the default GIF.
  • 🪪 Your level card shows its stats in full Voice time and XP on +rank and +lvl fit inside the card whatever the numbers: the line wraps onto two lines when needed.
  • 🛡️ Automatic MAX mode keeps your hardened security settings During a join wave, the bot turns on what is off and keeps any threshold no looser than the default. A threshold set too high (+antitoken 9999/1d) counts as off: another owner approves.
  • 💾 The off-server backup states its real schedule: 30 days The wizard, +offbackup and the help say “every 30 days”; with auto delivery off, +offbackup tells when the next manual backup is possible.
  • 👑 A restore keeps today's owner list +backup restore, the post-raid restore and re-inviting the bot keep the current owners; the first two say so in their report. To add one: +owner @member.
  • 🛡️ Adding an owner: the 2nd vote is now a button The other owners get the request by DM with Approve / Refuse, and the channel gets a “Vote” button for owners only. Every step is logged; +owner remove refuses a pending request.
  • 🎮 Steam review tracking works again for every game +steam add follows the given game (ID, link or name) and posts its new reviews. If Steam does not return the reviews, the message gives the real reason.
  • 🛒 Shop: a role for sale stays below staff and below its seller +shop addrole and +shop addtemprole only accept a role placed below every moderation role and below your highest role. A role, colour or custom role from +shop also stays below moderation.
  • 🏆 Hall of fame: record announcements are no longer lost A refused announcement is retried on the next record; a permission refusal is reported in the log channel, if set. A deleted channel is reported, and a hall of fame turned off shows its standings “on pause”.
  • 🛡️ Adding an owner: a new server owner can vote right away +owner add first checks that the person is a member of the server, and a request copy posted in a public channel no longer shows who made it (owner DMs still do).
  • 🛡️ Roles handed out by the bot never grant staff powers Menus, +autorole, +levelrole, custom commands, +quarantine lifts… refuse a role with a +perm tier, named in +cmdperm or placed above staff; the log channel says so.
  • 🛡️ A restore no longer turns a protection off without a 2nd owner +backup restore, raid recovery, +backup load, +config → Push and +importconfig keep on a critical protection the restored or copied value would turn off, and the report says so.
  • 🛡️ +punition: a clear alert when the anti-raid sanction changes The security log shows the sanction before and after, the modules and the command; a softening is flagged, with the exact command to go back, such as +punition all ban.
  • 🔊 +unmute also frees a member deafened by right-click +unmute now lifts the headphone deafen as well as the timeout and the microphone mute, and says what it lifted, what is still in place, or why it must wait until they are back in voice.
  • 📣 The bot's presentation is up to date The texts that present Hasu Protect (showcase server, bot lists) match the bot as it is: bilingual EN/FR, 240+ commands. +invite gives the link to add it.
  • 🔨 +tempban respects bans already in place On a member who is already banned, +tempban refuses and says so: only an owner can shorten an existing ban or make it temporary. Automatic sanctions no longer shorten it either.
  • 🛡️ A restore no longer softens the anti-raid sanction +backup restore, raid recovery, +backup load, +config → Push and +importconfig keep a module's sanction when the received value would soften it; the report says so.
  • ↩️ The ↩️ button of +warn follows the same rule as +sanctions del It only removes the warning of a member below you, and says why when it refuses or when there is nothing to remove, like +sanctions del.
  • 🛡️ No role is given while the block cannot be checked Unreadable +blrank or +bl list, unverifiable quarantine: levels, menus, shop and custom commands give nothing and say so; owners are warned.
  • 🛡️ A role given again is credited to whoever gave it again When a dangerous role that was taken back is given again, anti-nuke, the blacklist, Guardian and the log name the author of the new grant; when in doubt, “author not found”, and no one is sanctioned.
  • 🎫 Ticket commands only act in a ticket the bot opened +close, +rename, +claim, +add and +remove refuse a channel that only has a ticket name; quarantine appeals still work.
  • 🔒 +setup, +menu and the panel limited to owners Only the server owner, the owners added with +owner and the bot owners open the wizard, the panel and their buttons; to delegate: +owner @member.
  • 🔎 Channel log: each permission change names the right person The author shown is the one whose entry carries THAT change; a private channel opened to the whole server gets its own message, even with “Channels” unticked in +setup.
  • 🛡️ Servers no longer train Guardian's shared AI For owners: +wl, releases and sanctions no longer train the shared AI, and Allow / Refuse only tune Guardian on your server. Exception: a ban within 7 days after Guardian started watching.
  • 🔒 Alert buttons that act on a member are reserved for owners Quarantine, kick and remove-Administrator from +audit, and the compromised-account alert buttons: this server's owners only, on a target still flagged and ranked below them.
  • 📰 Clearer update announcements Each bot announcement is grouped by audience (owners, staff, members) and titled by what it contains. +news keeps the history.
  • 🎉 New level-up card It shows your progress to the next level, your rank and your new rank badge, on your banner as background. Admins set it up in +setup › Levels & XP.
  • 🌺 New rank “Island Beauty” at level 16 It sits between Elite and Champion. If ranks are already on in your server, run +grade sync to create the role: until then, your members keep Elite.
  • 🌱 Your moderators are no longer limited as new members A +perm level or permission to manage messages, time out, kick or ban is enough. Scam links stay removed for everyone, and the “new here” notice names progressive trust.
